title.narrative: Coalitions for Change Program Phase 3 - Philippines

description.narrative: Coalitions for Change Program Phase 3 (CfC3) is a grant to The Asia Foundation that builds on the success of previous phases. CfC3 works with formal and informal networks and coalitions to advocate for transformative policy reforms that improve the lives of Filipinos. The program will closely align with the priorities of Australia and the Philippines indicated in the Development Partnership Plan (2024-2028) and work with a wide range of local stakeholders and organisations.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: Australia contributed to the passing of the Ligtas Pinoy Centers Act (Safe Filipino Centers Act) (Republic Act No. 12076) in December 2024, in partnership with the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) under the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC). The law provides for a risk-informed approach to disaster preparedness, determining the location of evacuation centers based on hazard exposure and community vulnerability – reducing the scope for political influence. ‍ This reform was the result of long-term political engagement and expert advice from Agap Banta, a local advocacy group that Australia supported through the CfC program. Valued at AUD $44,000 (₱ 1.6 million), the reform helped develop criteria for site selection and inclusive design standards considering the needs of women, children, the elderly, and people with disabilities. The policy also lays a framework for implementing the government’s AUD $252 million (PHP 9 billion) annual allocation for the construction of permanent evacuation centers nationwide.

Australia is supporting the Philippine Government in tackling child stunting, an issue affecting nearly 30 per cent of Filipino children, through the Coalitions for Change program (CfC). CfC worked with the Malusog at Matalinong Bata (Healthy and Smart Child) coalition to support evidence-based analysis and political advocacy to generate the First 1000 Days (‘F1KD’) Grant reform. The F1KD Grant has been integrated with the Department of Social Welfare and Development’s (DSWD) 4Ps social protection program and now provides monthly cash transfers to pregnant women and families with children aged 0–2 – the group most vulnerable to undernutrition. Pregnant women must attend prenatal and postnatal check-ups and deliver in a health facility, while children must receive regular health visits and vaccinations to qualify. In its initial rollout this year, the government aims to benefit around 109,000 pregnant women and young children from eligible households who will receive ₱350 (AUD $9.45) per month. The grant is designed to reduce financial barriers to accessing maternal and child health services in low-income households and communities, supporting early development and future potential.
